page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g-120s is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core and 2 threads. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 120 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top tier. Geekbench single-core and text processing benchmarks also demonstrate strong results. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling into the lower tier. Memory bandwidth for large blocks and static web serving throughput perform at average levels, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and multi-threaded compiling show weaker performance.

The primary tradeoff of this instance is its high single-core efficiency contrasted against its weak multi-threaded and multi-core scaling due to the 2-vCPU limit. It represents a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require massive parallel processing but benefit from dedicated AMD EPYC CPU execution. This server is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale development environments.
